newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan copper smelter says water shortage over.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper smelter says water shortage over.

text.p: A water shortage that threatened copper output at Japan's Onahama Smelting and Refining Co has passed, after recent rains allowed the restoration of full water supplies, a spokesman for the company said on Wednesday.

Water supplies were cut by 30 percent last month due to a summer drought, although the spokesman said no production had been lost. He added it now appeared that full water supplies would be assured for the foreseeable future.
The Onahama copper refinery, owned by Mitsubishi Materials Corp and five other Japanese copper companies, is Japan's largest with a refining capacity of about 250,000 tonnes of cathodes per year.
